summary: Verified NPCEditor UI features on /rules → Bestiario → Animales → 'Gato'. Both new features work correctly and persist: (1) Armas tab shows 'Añadir ataque múltiple' button when empty, reveals textarea + 'Quitar' on add, and hides+clears on remove; (2) Defensa 'Habilidades' section allows adding a skill (Percepción +3, Sigilo +4) via the native select + modifier input + 'Añadir habilidad' button. Added skills are removed from the dropdown. Modifier editing and per-row trash button work. Save (PATCH /api/data/npcs/{id}) closes the modal and persists — reopening the creature detail shows the habilidades block (data-testid='npc-detail-habilidades-<id>') with 'Percepción +3, Sigilo +4' (plus a pre-existing legacy key 'percepcion +3' which was already in the record). 'Ataque Múltiple:' is NOT rendered in the detail card because it was left empty.

issues: Existing legacy habilidad key 'percepcion' (lowercase, unaccented) is displayed alongside the new 'Percepción'. Not caused by this feature, but users could end up with duplicates. Consider case-insensitive/normalized keys or a one-off migration to consolidate legacy skill keys.

action_items: Optional: normalize legacy habilidad keys (e.g. 'percepcion' → 'Percepción') to avoid showing duplicates when a creature already had legacy data.
critical_code_review_comments: NPCEditor.jsx (line ~89) spreads `formData` inside a useEffect dependent on `npc` only; because formData is not in deps, this is fine, but the shallow merge overwrites any user edits if `npc` reference changes mid-edit. Not blocking.
updateHabilidadMod allows the string '-' as a value in state which then gets sent to backend as a string, not a number. Consider coercing on save.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing 'Gato' creature (id 3ed11f24-d85b-443c-bc19-1898979fb5d7). After the test its habilidades were saved as {percepcion:3 (legacy), Percepción:3, Sigilo:4} and its ataque_multiple was left empty.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The 'Gato' creature now has two habilidades entries with visually similar names ('percepcion' and 'Percepción') because it already contained a legacy key before the feature was added. New saves via the editor use canonical names from ALL_SKILLS.
